title: Ames: faith-in-itself requires greater certainty than fiducia born from faith
source_text: CXXXVII. Praeterea indicat Amesius distinguendum esse, inter fidem in sese, & respectu actuum qui ad ejus essentiam requiruntur, consideratam; & inter fiduciam ex fide orientem, per quam vel praesens aliquod bonum apprehendimus, vel futurum speramus. Majorem autem certitudinis gradum in ipsa fide esse & requiri, quam in fiducia ex fide nascente, per quam, vel de bono praesenti, vel de futuro persuasi sumus; licet eadem fiducia, fidei quoque nomine designetur. Jam vero juxta Amesium, quum fideles dicuntur fide divina certi, vel de accepta gratia, vel de salute obtinenda, per fidem ibi intelligenda est, non fides justificans & salvifica in sese, sed fiducia ex fide oriens, per quam, vel apprehendimus jam concessam a Deo remissionem peccatorum, vel futuram salutem speramus. Proinde fiduciae isti, quae ex fide nascitur, ex mente Amesii minor competit certitudo, quam fidei, si in sese consideretur.
pass_a_gloss: Besides, Ames indicates that a distinction must be made between faith considered in itself and with respect to the acts which are required for its essence; and fiducia arising from faith, through which we either apprehend some present good or hope for a future one. But a greater degree of certainty is and is required in faith itself than in the fiducia born from faith, through which we are persuaded either concerning a present or a future good; although the same fiducia is also designated by the name of faith. Now indeed according to Ames, when the faithful are said to be certain by divine faith either concerning accepted grace or concerning salvation to be obtained, by faith there is to be understood not justifying and saving faith in itself, but fiducia arising from faith, through which we either apprehend remission of sins already granted by God or hope for future salvation. Therefore to that fiducia which is born from faith, according to Ames's mind, a lesser certainty belongs than to faith, if it be considered in itself.
pass_b_english: Ames further distinguishes faith-in-itself from fiducia that rises from faith — the trust by which we grasp a present good or hope a future one.
Greater certainty belongs to faith itself than to that born fiducia, even when the fiducia is loosely called faith.
So when believers are said to be divinely certain of accepted grace or coming salvation, Ames means fiducia from faith, not justifying faith as such — and that fiducia has lesser certainty.
